name: EWALU (エワル)
reasoning: I tried to break the 完全グルテンフリー専門店 claim by hunting Japanese blogs, Tabelog reviews and got-glutened reports and found none; multiple genuinely independent first-hand visitors (Tabelog reviewers, ameblo and inucafe bloggers) confirm the product line is 100% self-grown rice flour, and the shop is also listed as a completely-GF vendor in an independent Nagoya GF guide. Identity confirmed: rice-farmer cafe at 弥富市鯏浦町車東23-2, opened April 2024, open 9:00-17:00 closed Wednesdays, still trading. What I could NOT confirm is any celiac-grade handling protocol, whether every cafe/lunch-plate item (美活deliプレート, koji side dishes) is GF, or what is in the ordinary dog cookies sold on site — a dog-run cafe selling normal dog biscuits is a plausible wheat source on the premises. Holds at high, not dedicated.
red_flags: No published celiac cross-contamination protocol or dedicated-kitchen statement
Cafe sells ordinary dog cookies (普通の犬用クッキー) on site — dog biscuits are normally wheat-based; unverified whether wheat enters the premises through them
Independent visit write-up (inucafe-repobu) explicitly does NOT confirm that ALL cafe menu items are gluten-free — only the bagels/bread
The 大豆不使用 (no soy at all) claim is unusually broad and comes only from the shop itself; if soy sauce is used in any koji side dish that claim breaks
No FindMeGlutenFree / HappyCow celiac-grade review found
plain_rice: Likely yes — this is a rice farm's own cafe (onigiri planned/served, rice-based deli plate). Order unseasoned gohan only; do not assume the koji side dishes are safe.

name: Lilac (ライラック)
reasoning: I attacked this hardest on identity, because celiac.org lists a Lilac Patisserie that is the Santa Barbara CA bakery — a real confusion trap — but the FindMeGlutenFree listing I used resolves to 名古屋市千種区東山通1-15-2 / (052) 887-7818, matching the record exactly, so the celiac-grade corroboration is genuinely for the Nagoya shop. I could not find any got-glutened report, negative celiac review, closure notice or wheat-containing item: the shop's own site claims 小麦粉を一切使用しないオールグルテンフリー, Tokai TV (2025) independently reports 全ての商品に小麦粉を使用せず, FMGF reviewers call it a dedicated GF bakery, and naco — a Nagoya blogger with severe wheat allergy who cannot tolerate trace wheat, barley or oats — lists it as 全て小麦粉不使用. This clears the high bar comfortably and arguably clears dedicated; I left it at high because no shop-published cross-contamination or dedicated-facility protocol exists.
red_flags: No shop-published cross-contamination / dedicated-facility protocol; no wheat flour is a flour claim, not a facility audit
NAME COLLISION: celiac.org's Lilac Patisserie entry is the Santa Barbara, California bakery — do NOT cite it as corroboration for the Nagoya shop
Products contain dairy and butter — GF only, not allergen-free; vegan_status limited is correct
Takeout only, no seating; closed Wednesdays (one source) vs Mondays (another) — hours conflict, confirm before travelling

name: Vegedeco Salad Lab (ベジデコサラダラボ)
reasoning: Per the dressing brief I went after the dressings and the record's evidence base collapsed: the CNN/BBC recognition cited as a positive is the company's OWN media page, and both broadcasts covered the salad-cake visual novelty with no GF or allergen content, while the prtimes item is the company's own press release — so the independent count is effectively one local visit write-up (jouhou.nagoya). The GF framing here is 低糖質・ノンシュガー lifestyle marketing around a registered trademark, not celiac safety: no allergen statement, no cross-contact protocol, and the beet/koji/cocoa dressings and the marinated cabbage and carrot have NO published ingredient list, so wheat soy sauce in a dressing or marinade cannot be excluded. Damningly, the shop is absent from both Nagoya gluten-free guides I checked, including one compiled by a blogger with severe wheat allergy who cannot tolerate trace amounts.
red_flags: SOURCE INFLATION: internationally recognised gluten-free specialist (CNN, BBC) is sourced to the company's own media page; the BBC 2018 and CNN 2017 segments were tourism/visual-novelty features with no GF or allergen content
prtimes.jp entry is the company's own press release, not independent corroboration
Dressings (ビーツドレッシング, 糀ドレッシング, ココアドレッシング) and the marinated cabbage/carrot have no published ingredients — wheat soy sauce in a dressing or marinade is not excluded
GF is positioned as a 低糖質/ノンシュガー health-trend trademark (ベジデコサラダ®), not as celiac accommodation; no allergen or cross-contact statement anywhere
Absent from both independent Nagoya gluten-free guides checked, including one by a severe wheat-allergy blogger who vets shops for trace exposure
Only 1 Tabelog review; retail open Fri/Sat/Sun 11:00-18:00 only — very low third-party footprint to audit against
Not all items uniform: the sweet potato tart is reported to contain egg, so a blanket every-item-is-the-same claim is false
identity_note: Business identity confirmed (株式会社Mitsuki Style takeout shop, 昭和区花見通1-96, near 川名 station, opened July 2018, still listed as open) — but note it is primarily a cooking-class studio; the retail counter runs only Fri-Sun and the shop's own /lab/ page presents the address as a classroom, so a visitor may find no retail service.

name: HAPPY SMILE KOMEKO (ハッピースマイルこめこ)
reasoning: I tried to find a second genuinely independent source and could not: both cited write-ups (bagel-atsume and nara.goguynet) are November 2025 opening announcements reprinting the shop's own launch copy, there is no FindMeGlutenFree/HappyCow/celiac corroboration anywhere, and when I fetched the shop's only official channel (Instagram, which the record uses as its website) the visible bio does not surface an explicit グルテンフリー or 米粉100% statement at all. Against that sits a concrete unresolved wheat vector the record itself flagged and nobody has closed: the 焦がしみたらし×チーズ bagel, since mitarashi glaze is soy-sauce based and default Japanese soy sauce is wheat; the bacon epi is a second unverified processed-meat vector. This is a two-days-a-week micro-bakery that opened nine months ago and also runs bread classes on the same premises, with zero published allergen handling. One source cannot support high — capped at options.
red_flags: 焦がしみたらし×チーズ bagel — mitarashi glaze is soy-sauce based; wheat soy sauce is not excluded by any source
Bacon epi: Japanese processed bacon seasoning can carry wheat; no ingredient disclosure
Both independent sources are reprints of the same November 2025 opening announcement — not independent corroboration
Shop's own Instagram bio does not surface an explicit gluten-free / 100%-rice-flour claim; the claim reaches us only second-hand
Brand-new (opened 7 Nov 2025) owner-operated micro-bakery, open only Tue and Sun from 12:00; also hosts baking classes on the premises
Address discrepancy between sources: 紀寺町565-1 (local news) vs 紀寺町585-1 (Instagram bio) — verify before travelling
No celiac-grade review on any GF platform
identity_note: Business exists and is trading, but the street number differs between the local news article (紀寺町565-1) and the Instagram bio (紀寺町585-1); confirm the address before sending anyone.

name: laccola (ラッコラ)
reasoning: The record's headline quote すべての商品がグルテンフリー is attributed to the shop, but reading laccola.com and the laccola.base.shop storefront directly, the shop makes NO blanket all-products-gluten-free claim — it brands itself vegan & glutenfree sweets and states 小麦・卵・乳製品・白砂糖は不使用 on individual items only; that blanket quote actually traces to komeko-palette.com, which is a rival rice-flour bread e-commerce site running an SEO listicle, not an independent auditor. That leaves the Yahoo News/ナラクロ opening piece as the single genuinely independent source, which cannot support high. Compounding it: laccola sells an entire オートミールクッキー category and nowhere on the site, the storefront or any source is there a certified-gluten-free-oat sourcing statement — in Japan oats are routinely milled alongside wheat and barley, so this is a live gluten vector, not a theoretical one. Mildly reassuring counter-finding: the product-level 特定原材料 allergen notices name almonds, soy and tree nuts but never 小麦, consistent with a wheat-free workshop.
red_flags: MISATTRIBUTED QUOTE: すべての商品がグルテンフリー is not on laccola's own site; it comes from komeko-palette.com, a competing rice-flour bread retailer's SEO guide
Full オートミールクッキー product category with no certified-GF-oat sourcing statement — oats in Japan are a standard wheat/barley cross-contamination vector
Product pages carry 製造所ではアレルゲン特定原材料等を含む材料を使用しています — a shared-facility allergen disclaimer (it names almonds/soy/nuts, not wheat, but it is still an uncontrolled-facility notice)
No cross-contamination, dedicated-workshop or allergen-handling protocol published anywhere
No FindMeGlutenFree / HappyCow celiac-grade review located; the apparent FMGF hit was a search-engine paraphrase, not a verified listing
Closed Sun/Mon/Tue — narrow visiting window
identity_note: Identity confirmed — vegan & gluten-free patisserie at 奈良市西大寺東町2-1-4, opened 29 July 2022, open 11:00-17:30 Wed-Sat, physical shop plus BASE online store. The old laccola.wixsite.com URL now 301-redirects to laccola.com.
